# Hook reference

<!-- Generated by `bun run docs:hooks` (tools/hooks-reference.ts). Do not edit by hand: edit the docblock at the call site and regenerate. CI fails when this file is stale. -->

Every action and filter the plugin fires, read from `src/`: 26 actions and 38 filters of its own, plus 2 WordPress core hooks it fires, across 76 call sites. Naming conventions for new hooks are in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#hook-conventions).

Feature guides with examples: [extending the login UI](extending-the-login-ui.md), [change email](change-email.md), [password reset](password-reset.md), [identity linking](identity-linking.md), [rate limiting](rate-limiting.md).

## Actions

| Hook | Summary | Since |
|---|---|---|
| [`workos_account_split_detected`](#workos_account_split_detected) | Fires when a WorkOS user is linked to one WP user while its email belongs to another. | 1.0.12 |
| [`workos_activity_logged`](#workos_activity_logged) | Fires after an activity event is logged. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_authkit_enqueue_assets`](#workos_authkit_enqueue_assets) | Fires after the AuthKit bundle is enqueued for a profile. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_bypass_activated`](#workos_bypass_activated) | Fires when login bypass is activated. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_change_email_cancelled`](#workos_change_email_cancelled) | Fires after a pending change is cancelled. | 1.0.6 |
| [`workos_change_email_confirmed`](#workos_change_email_confirmed) | Fires after an email change is committed to WorkOS + WP. Shared with the verified-confirm path so downstream observers don't have to special-case how the change was authorized. | 1.0.6 |
| [`workos_change_email_conflict_detected`](#workos_change_email_conflict_detected) | Fired before the policy is enforced so other features (notably the future merge flow in Issue 2) can observe the collision. | 1.0.6 |
| [`workos_change_email_initiated`](#workos_change_email_initiated) | Fires after a pending email change is stored and notifications sent. | 1.0.6 |
| [`workos_change_email_merge_requested`](#workos_change_email_merge_requested) | Fired when the conflict policy is `merge_request`. The future merge feature (Issue 2) subscribes here. Until that lands the request still rejects, mirroring `block`. | 1.0.6 |
| [`workos_login_denied`](#workos_login_denied) | Fires when a login is denied by the entitlement gate. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_login_profile_deleted`](#workos_login_profile_deleted) | Fires after a Login Profile is deleted. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_login_profile_saved`](#workos_login_profile_saved) | Fires after a Login Profile is saved. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_logout_redirect_before`](#workos_logout_redirect_before) | Fires just before the role-based logout redirect is applied. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_logout_redirect_skipped`](#workos_logout_redirect_skipped) | Fires when role-based logout redirect is skipped. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_org_membership_changed`](#workos_org_membership_changed) | Fires after a user's local organization membership is added, changed or removed. | 1.0.10 |
| [`workos_redirect_before`](#workos_redirect_before) | Fires just before the role-based redirect is applied. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_redirect_skipped`](#workos_redirect_skipped) | Fires when role-based redirect is skipped. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_user_authenticated`](#workos_user_authenticated) | Fires after a user is authenticated via WorkOS. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_user_created`](#workos_user_created) | Fires when a brand-new WP user is created via WorkOS authentication. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_user_link_refused`](#workos_user_link_refused) | Fires when Re-link Protection refuses to move a WP user to a different WorkOS user. | 1.0.10 |
| [`workos_user_linked`](#workos_user_linked) | Fires when a WP user is linked to a WorkOS user it wasn't linked to before. | 1.0.10 |
| [`workos_webhook`](#workos_webhook) | Fires for all WorkOS webhook events. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_webhook_{$event_type}`](#workos_webhook_event_type) | Fires for each verified WorkOS webhook event the plugin handles, named after the WorkOS event type with its dots kept (`workos_webhook_user.updated`, `workos_webhook_dsync.user.created`, …). | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos_webhook_user.updated`](#workos_webhook_userupdated) | Re-fires a directory `dsync.user.updated` event as `user.updated`. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos/container/registered_provider`](#workoscontainerregistered_provider) | Fires when any service provider is registered. | 1.0.0 |
| [`workos/container/registered_provider:{static::class}`](#workoscontainerregistered_providerstaticclass) | Fires after one specific controller registers, with the controller's fully qualified class name as the suffix (`workos/container/registered_provider:WorkOS\Sync\Controller`). | 1.0.0 |

## Details

### `workos_account_split_detected`

Action, since 1.0.12.

Fires when a WorkOS user is linked to one WP user while its email belongs to another.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$linked_id` | `int` | WP user linked to the WorkOS user. |
| `$holder_id` | `int` | WP user that has the WorkOS user's email. |
| `$workos_user` | `array` | WorkOS user data. |
| `$source` | `string` | What is signing in or syncing. |
| `$refused` | `bool` | Whether the sign-in was refused. |

Fired from: [`Sync/UserSync.php:269`](../src/WorkOS/Sync/UserSync.php#L269).

### `workos_change_email_confirmed`

Action, since 1.0.6.

Fires after an email change is committed to WorkOS + WP. Shared with the verified-confirm path so downstream observers don't have to special-case how the change was authorized.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$user_id` | `int` | Target WP user ID. |
| `$old_email` | `string` | Previous email. |
| `$new_email` | `string` | New email. |

Fired from: [`Auth/ChangeEmail/RestApi.php:476`](../src/WorkOS/Auth/ChangeEmail/RestApi.php#L476), [`Auth/ChangeEmail/RestApi.php:602`](../src/WorkOS/Auth/ChangeEmail/RestApi.php#L602).

### `workos_change_email_conflict_detected`

Action, since 1.0.6.

Fired before the policy is enforced so other features (notably the future merge flow in Issue 2) can observe the collision.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$target_user_id` | `int` | User whose email is changing. |
| `$new_email` | `string` | Requested new address. |
| `$conflicting_user_id` | `int` | Existing WP user that owns the address. |
| `$policy` | `string` | Resolved policy slug. |

Fired from: [`Auth/ChangeEmail/ConflictResolver.php:77`](../src/WorkOS/Auth/ChangeEmail/ConflictResolver.php#L77).

### `workos_change_email_merge_requested`

Action, since 1.0.6.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$target_user_id` | `int` | User whose email is changing. |
| `$new_email` | `string` | Requested new address. |
| `$conflicting_user_id` | `int` | Existing WP user that owns the address. |

Fired from: [`Auth/ChangeEmail/ConflictResolver.php:104`](../src/WorkOS/Auth/ChangeEmail/ConflictResolver.php#L104).

### `workos_webhook_{$event_type}`

Action, since 1.0.0.

Fires for each verified WorkOS webhook event the plugin handles, named after the WorkOS event type with its dots kept (`workos_webhook_user.updated`, `workos_webhook_dsync.user.created`, …). The dots mirror WorkOS event names on purpose; it is the one exception to the snake_case naming convention. The event types are the `$handlers` list in `Webhook\Receiver::handle()`. Use `workos_webhook` to see every event.

Fires for a specific WorkOS webhook event type.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `$event` | `array` | Full event payload. |

Fired from: [`Webhook/Receiver.php:139`](../src/WorkOS/Webhook/Receiver.php#L139).

Names the plugin listens to itself: `workos_webhook_dsync.group.user_added`, `workos_webhook_dsync.group.user_removed`, `workos_webhook_dsync.user.created`, `workos_webhook_dsync.user.deleted`, `workos_webhook_dsync.user.updated`, `workos_webhook_organization.created`, `workos_webhook_organization.updated`, `workos_webhook_organization_membership.created`, `workos_webhook_organization_membership.deleted`, `workos_webhook_organization_membership.updated`, `workos_webhook_user.created`, `workos_webhook_user.deleted`, `workos_webhook_user.updated`.
